clue.text: Something in class making one gloomy and uninterested when heard

indicators.note: when heard tells us the words are spoken, so we write what they sound like

parts.note: gloomy means black and uninterested means bored, giving black bored

explanation.surface: A pupil complains that school leaves them depressed and bored.
explanation.walkthrough: BLACK (gloomy) plus BORED (uninterested), said aloud, sounds like the thing on the classroom wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark writing board found at the front of a schoolroom is something in a class.

clue.text: Float on air, no thanks to the priest

indicators.note: no here tells us a word for thanks is taken away from the float word

parts.note: to float on air is to levitate
ta is informal British for thanks

explanation.surface: A clergyman drifts upward, owing nothing to anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove TA from LEVITATE, the verb for 'Float on air'; the indicator is 'no'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Levite was a member of the Hebrew tribe that served as priestly assistants in the Temple.

clue.text: Most of the bullfight, or all of the gallery

indicators.note: most of means the Spanish word for a bullfight loses its final letter

parts.note: a corrida is a Spanish bullfight
taken as written, all of it

explanation.surface: A spectator chooses between part of a bullfight or a whole art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: CORRID (CORRIDA without its last letter) + OR, where 'all of' says the word or is used entire.
explanation.definitionFit: A long passage or covered walkway can be called a gallery.

clue.text: Secondary route — British Rail uses one in Channel storms

parts.note: BR is the abbreviation for British Rail, the former UK national railway

indicators.note: in shows the letter for one goes inside the jumbled letters
storms means the letters of Channel are tossed about into a new order

parts.note: the Roman numeral I stands for one

explanation.surface: A railway operator's ferry route across the English Channel in bad weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'storms' makes ANCHLNE, and 'in' then places the numeral within it to give ANCHLINE. Branch lines were the minor routes of Britain's old railways.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor railway track leading off the main one is a secondary route.

clue.text: Is French in a leading position as a language?

indicators.note: in places the French verb inside the word for the front position

parts.note: the van is the front or leading position, as in vanguard
est is French for is

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the French language leads the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a leading position' reads as 'in the van', the front of an army. 'as' and the second 'a' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Avestan is the ancient Iranian tongue of the Zoroastrian scriptures.

clue.text: The German capturing English is a beast

indicators.note: capturing means the German article holds the letter for English inside it

parts.note: der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: A German speaker who seizes an Englishman is called a brute.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag or doe is an animal, a beast of the field.

clue.text: Forceful character in the market, one after financial deductions

parts.note: a mart is a market
the Roman numeral I stands for one
a net sum is what remains after tax and other deductions

explanation.surface: A tough trader in the market counts what is left after tax.
explanation.definitionFit: A strict disciplinarian who demands obedience is a forceful character.

clue.text: When moving round it could produce grist — no end!

definitions.text: When moving round it could produce grist — no end!

indicators.note: moving round tells us the letters spin into a new order, like a turning millstone

explanation.surface: A mill wheel turns and turns, grinding out endless corn for the miller.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal is 'moving round'; GRIST and NO END rearranged give the stone that, turning, grinds grist without end.
explanation.definitionFit: A revolving stone for grinding or sharpening; grist is grain for milling.

clue.text: Extract from Rene Clair film, a light confection

indicators.note: extract from tells us the letters are found running inside the director's name

explanation.surface: A clip from a French director's film is offered like a dainty pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: René Clair was a French film director; the letters run across his two names.
explanation.definitionFit: A choux pastry filled with cream and iced with chocolate is a light sweet confection.

clue.text: Have too high an opinion of bowlers' speed

definitions.text: Have too high an opinion of

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls delivered by a bowler
rate means speed

explanation.surface: A cricket fan thinks the bowling is overpraised for its pace.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, bowlers deliver the ball in sets of six called overs.
explanation.definitionFit: To value something more highly than it deserves is to overvalue it.

clue.text: Town boy goes round old city, boring part

indicators.note: goes round means the word for boy encloses the other pieces

parts.note: a son is a boy
Ur is the ancient Sumerian city, a crossword favourite
a bit is the part of a drill that bores

explanation.surface: A lad walks around an old city and finds it dull.
explanation.walkthrough: SURBITON is a suburban town in south-west London. 'boring' means drilling, not dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Surbiton is a suburb in Greater London, a town by the Thames.

clue.text: A number died, nurse

parts.note: ten is a number
d is the abbreviation for died, used in genealogies

explanation.surface: Several patients died, and a nurse is left to cope.
explanation.definitionFit: To nurse someone is to look after or care for them.

clue.text: It may offer quick protection

parts.note: the quick is the tender flesh under a nail, so this covers an injured digit rather than offering speedy defence

explanation.definitionFit: A sheath worn over an injured thumb guards the sensitive flesh beneath the nail.

clue.text: Receivers, being hard-headed, need a shop for distribution

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as in pencil grades

indicators.note: for distribution tells us the letters are spread out and reordered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Stubborn retailers need a shop to sell their audio gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hard-headed' tells us the letter for hard heads the answer; the rearranged letters (EADPHONES) follow it.
explanation.definitionFit: Earphones worn over the head pick up sound signals, so they are receivers.

clue.text: Fail, wanting support to re-invest

parts.note: to plough is British slang for failing an exam
to back is to support

explanation.surface: Someone who flunks out needs backing before putting money in again.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'plough' an exam is old British slang for failing it.
explanation.definitionFit: To return profits into a business rather than paying them out is to reinvest them.

clue.text: Find fault with dreadful pub — surprise visit by cops follows

indicators.note: follows puts the police word after the jumbled letters
dreadful here signals that the letters of pub are made a mess of

parts.note: a raid is a surprise visit by police

explanation.surface: A terrible pub is raided by police and duly criticised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dreadful' gives UPB, and 'follows' puts the police word after it.
explanation.definitionFit: To scold or reproach someone is to criticise them.

clue.text: Drew blood without skin becoming brown and streaky

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the bleeding word goes round the skin word

parts.note: bled means drew blood
rind is skin, as of fruit or cheese

explanation.surface: A wound draws blood without breaking the skin, turning brown and streaked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking: the bleeding word wraps round the skin word.
explanation.definitionFit: Brindled describes an animal's coat that is tawny with darker streaks.

clue.text: Nelson's hard speech with no end of expectation

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as in pencil grades

indicators.note: with no tells us a letter is removed from the word for speech

parts.note: an oration is a formal speech

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the word expectation

explanation.surface: Nelson's famous signal before Trafalgar, about England's expectation, is recalled as a tough speech.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove N, the last letter of 'expectation', from ORATION. The surface recalls Nelson's signal 'England expects'.
explanation.definitionFit: Admiral Lord Nelson's first name; the possessive marks the name belonging to him.

clue.text: Plant house has spade carelessly left outside

indicators.note: has means the jumbled tool word holds the house abbreviation within it
carelessly means the letters of spade are thrown into disorder

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left, here set on the outer end of the rest

explanation.surface: A gardener leaves a spade lying out by the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carelessly' gives ASPDE from the tool's letters, and 'has' tucks the house letters within (ASPHODE); 'house' is the common abbreviation, not a building.
explanation.definitionFit: The asphodel is a lily-like flower, legendarily growing in the Elysian fields.

clue.text: Pirates at sea for money

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of pirates are jumbled

explanation.surface: Buccaneers sail the oceans in search of treasure.
explanation.definitionFit: A piastre is a coin or currency unit used in Egypt, Lebanon and elsewhere.

clue.text: Very happy group of people talking foolishly

parts.note: blithe means carefree and joyful
a ring is a group of people, often a gang

explanation.surface: A cheerful circle of friends chatters away about nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To blither is to babble nonsense, so this means prattling or rambling idiotically.

clue.text: With due deference to piano expert

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: Bowing respectfully to a master pianist.
explanation.walkthrough: PACE is Latin, used in English to politely disagree with someone named.
explanation.definitionFit: Used formally before a name to mean with respect to the opinion of that person.

clue.text: Individual wearing hat is a gangster

parts.note: a cap is a hat
one means an individual

explanation.surface: A lone figure in a fedora turns out to be a mobster.
explanation.walkthrough: Al Capone was the notorious Chicago gangster.
explanation.definitionFit: Al Capone ran organised crime in Prohibition-era Chicago.

clue.text: The normal channels for main changes of direction

explanation.surface: Official routes are rerouted for big changes in policy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'main' is the sea: the ebb and flow of tides change direction. Tideways are channels the tide normally runs in.
explanation.definitionFit: Channels the sea flows along regularly; also, the routes by which the ocean's currents reverse with ebb and flow.

clue.text: A cyst is coming up in a different place

indicators.note: in a down entry coming up means the cyst word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a wen is a cyst on the skin

explanation.surface: A lump keeps appearing somewhere else on the body.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, 'is coming up' reads the cyst word from the bottom, giving NEW.
explanation.definitionFit: Afresh, starting again, perhaps in a new way or location.

clue.text: Rush, accompanying doc to operation — little sign of emotion?

parts.note: to tear is to rush
Dr is the abbreviation for doctor, informally doc

explanation.surface: A patient hurries with the doctor into surgery, a tear in their eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A single drop shed when crying is a small outward show of feeling.

clue.text: Architectural ribbing can get royal personage into a row

indicators.note: into means the royal letters are put inside the row word

parts.note: a line is a row
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Joking about architecture can land a queen in a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ribbing' looks like teasing and 'row' like a quarrel; both are architectural and orderly here.
explanation.definitionFit: A lierne is a short tertiary rib in Gothic vaulting connecting the main ribs.

clue.text: We'd like smashing bit of lawn? Little hesitation to get this!

definitions.text: We'd like smashing bit of lawn? Little hesitation to get this!

indicators.note: smashing means the letters of the preceding words are broken up and reassembled
bit of picks just the first letter of lawn

parts.note: er is a short hesitating sound

explanation.surface: A gardener hesitates over a ruined lawn and reaches for a remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smashing' rearranges WEDLIKE plus L (from 'bit of lawn') to WEEDKILL, and ER follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A herbicide destroys unwanted plants, which a gardener would buy to clear a patchy lawn.
